caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: This line plot, titled “SST-2, dirty-label, poison_num: 16,” illustrates the ASR (Attack Success Rate) performance of three different trigger insertion strategies — “start” (teal line with circle markers), “random” (orange line with cross markers), and “end” (purple line with circle markers) — across a set of trigger words displayed on the x-axis. The x-axis lists nine trigger words: “bb”, “mb”, “cf”, “beautiful”, “excellent”, “gorgeous”, “wonderful”, “brilliant”, “stunning”, and “beautifully”, arranged in ascending order of the clean model’s ASR (as noted in the caption), though the axis itself is categorical and not numerically scaled. The y-axis, labeled “ASR”, is linear and ranges from 0.0 to approximately 0.9, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The “start” trigger (teal) begins at ~0.73 for “bb”, drops sharply to ~0.16 at “mb”, then rises steadily to ~0.91 at “beautifully”. The “random” trigger (orange) starts at ~0.13 for “bb”, dips to ~0.10 at “mb”, then climbs progressively to ~0.89 at “beautifully”. The “end” trigger (purple) begins at ~0.40 for “bb”, rises to ~0.44 at “mb”, spikes to ~0.90 at “cf”, dips to ~0.62 at “beautiful”, then fluctuates before reaching ~0.91 at “beautifully”. All three lines generally trend upward across the trigger words, with the “end” strategy showing the most volatility and the highest peak early on, while “start” and “random” show smoother, more consistent growth toward the end.
